svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.23 WOOD-FRAME CONSTRUCTION
Roof Trusses

g.text: Truss designed to good engineering practice, (1).
Continuous lateral bracing anchored to the roof
and ceiling diaphragms at 6.10 m o.c. or less.
All bracing as per the truss design drawings, (3)
Good engineering practice such as that described in TPIC 2019, “Truss Design Procedures and Specifications for
Light Metal Plate Connected Wood Trusses.”
Joint connections designed in conformance with the requirements in Subsection 4.3.1. (See Note
All member bracing installed as per the truss design drawings.

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Wood roof trusses are designed in accordance
with good engineering practice such as that
described in TPIC 2019, “Truss Design
Procedures and Specifications for Light Metal
Plate Connected Wood Trusses.”
The joint connections used in trusses
described in Sentence (1) are designed in
conformance with the requirements in
Subsection 4.3.1. (See Note A-9.23.14.11.(2).)
All member bracing is installed as per the
truss design drawings, and continuous lateral
bracing is adequately anchored to the roof and
ceiling diaphragms at intervals no greater
Drawn: Fink trusses at 600 mm o.c., slope 1 in 1. Plates, brace positions and the diagonal anchorage are illustration only. Follow the truss design drawings.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.14.11. (page 9-222)
